## Must fix before opening

**F1 · P2 · Medium (I3×L2) · CONFIRMED, confidence 90**
`src/modules/balances/datasources/zerion-balances-api.service.ts:330-333`

- **What:** `_fetchChainMappings` (`:356-391`, not changed here) sets `chainMappingsInitialized = true` even when the mainnet or testnet fetch fails. That network's mapping then stays `{}` until the process restarts.
- **Before this change:** every affected request threw a plain `Error`. `GlobalErrorFilter` turned it into a 500 and logged it at `error` level (`global-error.filter.ts:37-42`), so alerts fired.
- **Now:** the same case logs a `warn` and returns 422 through `HttpExceptionNoLog`. Nothing between the datasource and the controller logs it at error level (checked in `balances.repository.ts` and `balances.service.ts`).
- **What happens:** one brief Zerion `/v1/chains` failure on first use breaks counterfactual balances on that network for the life of the process. That covers every chain without `balancesProvider.chainName`, and the field can be null (`chain.schema.ts:64-69`). No error is ever logged, and it looks exactly like "Zerion doesn't support this chain".
- **Fix:** don't set `chainMappingsInitialized` when a network's fetch failed, or retry that network later. Another option is to throw a 5xx or log at error level when the mapping for the requested network is empty, as opposed to a mapping that loaded but doesn't contain the chain.

## Worth a ticket or your call

| ID | Pri | Area | Location | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F2 | P3 | Bugs | `src/modules/balances/datasources/zerion-balances-api.service.ts:206` | In `getCollectibles`, `_getChainName` runs inside the `try`. The new `HttpExceptionNoLog` is caught there and rewrapped by `httpErrorFactory.from()` as a 503 "Service unavailable". So an unsupported chain still returns 503 for collectibles but 422 for balances. Collectibles also gains a `warn` log that didn't exist before, because `DataSourceErrorFilter` never logged these. |
| F3 | P3 | Testing | `src/modules/balances/datasources/zerion-balances-api.service.spec.ts:200-202`, `src/modules/positions/datasources/zerion-positions-api.service.spec.ts:376-378` | `rejects.toThrow(new HttpExceptionNoLog(...))` only compares the message in Jest. The 422 status and the exception class are not asserted, so switching back to `throw Error(message)` would still pass. Add `.rejects.toBeInstanceOf(HttpExceptionNoLog)` plus a `getStatus()` check, or add a controller-level test expecting 422. |
| F4 | P3 | Regression | `src/modules/balances/datasources/zerion-balances-api.service.ts:333`, `src/modules/positions/datasources/zerion-positions-api.service.ts:241` | The public balances and positions endpoints now return 422 where they returned 500. Web and mobile clients that retry or show different UI depending on 4xx vs 5xx will behave differently. This is probably intended; confirm with the client teams or mention it in the PR description. |
| F5 | P3 | KISS | `src/modules/positions/datasources/zerion-positions-api.service.ts:240` | `ZerionChainMappingService.getNetworkFromChainId` already warns `Unknown chain ID for Zerion mapping` (`zerion-chain-mapping.service.ts:82`). The new warn means each unsupported-chain positions request logs two warnings. |
| F6 | P3 | Conventions | `src/modules/balances/datasources/zerion-balances-api.service.ts:333`, `src/modules/positions/datasources/zerion-positions-api.service.ts:241` | For non-network errors these datasources already throw `DataSourceError(message, code)` (for example unsupported currency at `:123` and positions `:85`). `DataSourceErrorFilter` doesn't log those. `new DataSourceError(message, 422)` would give the same result without bringing a route-layer `HttpException` into the datasource layer. |
